jobs.title: Chief Information Officer
jobs.description:
Company Description
Alfa Capital Management is a premier capital management firm delivering high-quality financial services to individual and institutional clients. The firm offers a broad range of solutions, including investment and portfolio management, hedge fund and wealth management services, private equity and alternative investments, and quantitative research–driven advisory. By combining traditional investment principles with advanced quantitative models, Alfa Capital Management designs data-driven strategies focused on performance and risk control. Its disciplined, research-based approach emphasizes personalized investment strategies, quantitative risk management, strategic asset allocation, and dynamic portfolio optimization. The firm is committed to transparent, client-centric service, aiming to create sustainable wealth and financial security across market cycles.
Role Description
The Chief Information Officer (CIO) is a full-time, remote role responsible for leading Alfa Capital Management’s information technology vision, strategy, and operations. The CIO will oversee the design, implementation, and optimization of technology platforms that support investment management, quantitative research, risk analytics, and core business functions. Day-to-day responsibilities include directing IT operations, ensuring system reliability and cybersecurity, managing vendor relationships, and aligning technology initiatives with business objectives and regulatory requirements. The CIO will collaborate with executive leadership to drive digital transformation, enhance data governance, and support scalable infrastructure for trading, portfolio management, and client reporting. This role also includes building and mentoring IT teams, setting performance standards, and promoting continuous improvement in processes and technology capabilities.
Qualifications

Strong foundation in Information Technology, including enterprise systems, infrastructure, and cybersecurity.
Proven experience in IT Operations, including service delivery, incident management, and systems administration.
Demonstrated expertise in IT Management, team leadership, budgeting, and vendor oversight.
Ability to develop and execute IT Strategy aligned with business goals and regulatory requirements.
Experience optimizing Business Processes through technology, automation, and data-driven workflows.
Background in financial services or capital markets, with familiarity in trading, risk, and portfolio systems preferred.
Excellent communication, stakeholder management, and decision-making skills in cross-functional environments.
Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field; relevant certifications (e.g., CISSP, ITIL, PMP) are a plus.

jobs.title: Director, Core IT Integration Delivery Lead
jobs.description:
Job Description

Grant Thornton is seeking a Director, Core IT Integration Delivery Lead to join the team. Approved office locations can be found below.

Grant Thornton GTech’s vision is centered around enabling scalable, secure, and repeatable technology integration for acquired companies. The Core IT Integration Office is responsible for integrating acquired firms into the firm’s enterprise technology environment through a standardized, factory-style model that is governed centrally, executed through partners and in-country teams, and repeatable across the acquisition portfolio.

The Director, Core IT Integration - Technical Delivery Lead owns end-to-end technical delivery across the portfolio. The role is directly accountable for five Core IT components: tenant consolidation, ServiceNow, data migration and archival, network security, and branch office integration. It leads the workstream leads who own each of those components, sets sequencing and architecture direction across them, and manages the implementation partners and in-country resources that perform the work. Seven further Core IT components are delivered by Information Security, People & Culture, and Finance. This role does not deliver those, but is accountable for the sequencing seams between them and its own scope, so that dependencies hold and no entity stalls waiting on an unmanaged handoff.

Execution is delivered through implementation partners and regional resources. The Grant Thornton team owns the standard, the plan, the readiness decisions, the quality of what is delivered, and the outcome for the business. This role directs partner delivery rather than performing it, and is expected to know the technology well enough to review designs, question estimates, validate results, and make decisions under pressure. Scope decisions anchor to four tests: security, cost optimization, standardization, and enabling Global Delivery Center support.

Essential Duties & Responsibilities:

Own the integrated technical delivery plan across the acquisition portfolio, sequencing entities into waves that balance entity priority, size, readiness, dependency, partner capacity, and business impact.
Manage concurrency across entities so that parallel execution stays within the delivery system’s throughput, and re-sequence when readiness, funding, or partner capacity changes.
Own delivery of tenant consolidation, covering migration of acquired Microsoft 365 and Entra tenants into the Grant Thornton tenant, including identity, mail, collaboration content, device management, and associated Azure subscription and workload moves.
Own delivery of ServiceNow onboarding for acquired entities, covering configuration data, service catalog and fulfillment alignment, support group structures, integrations, and transition into the enterprise support model.
Own delivery of data migration and archival, covering the Snowflake-based pipelines that feed system migrations and the durable archival of legacy data for retention, compliance, and future reuse.
Own delivery of network security, covering the Zero-Trust landing zone, regional hub readiness, segmentation, routing, and secure remote access for each acquisition.
Own delivery of branch office integration, covering connectivity, local network and endpoint baseline, site readiness, and retirement of inherited network infrastructure.
Coordinate with the owners of the remaining Core IT components, including identity directory sync, workforce systems, identity governance, security integration phases, intranet, and financial consolidation, managing dependencies and sequencing across those boundaries.
Sequence delivery to run concurrent with Information Security’s phased model rather than behind it, and manage the dependency under which full identity-driven security controls complete only after tenant consolidation.
Hold security review and sign-off as a gate before interconnect and go-live, and resist schedule pressure to bypass it.
Coordinate with the customer relationship management workstream and other capability programs that depend on Core IT sequencing, including where staffing sits outside this team.
Own and mature the integration factory model, increasing the share of each integration that runs to a standard pattern and reducing the variable component that drives cost and schedule risk.
Own the per-entity estimating model, including size banding, and maintain its accuracy by testing estimates against actuals as entities complete.
Manage cost per user and cost per entity as governed delivery metrics, working with partners and sourcing to improve unit economics as volume grows.
Prepare cost estimates, business cases, and variance analysis to support funding decisions made by Integration Office and Chief Technology Office leadership.
Direct implementation partners, systems integrators, and in-country resources through design, build, migration, cutover, and stabilization, holding delivery to enterprise standards, committed dates, and quality expectations.
Review and challenge partner designs, bills of materials, effort estimates, and delivery plans before acceptance, and confirm that what is proposed matches the standard rather than the partner’s default approach.
Support scoping, statement of work development, and commercial negotiation for integration partners, in coordination with sourcing, legal, and Integration Office leadership.
Evaluate delivery partners by region and workstream, maintaining competitive tension, regional coverage, and the ability to scale capacity up and down as the wave plan requires.
Establish readiness gates for each entity covering identity, data, endpoint, application, security, communications, and support coverage, and hold cutover decisions to documented evidence.
Lead cutover execution across workstreams, including runbooks, command center operations, go and no-go decisions, escalation paths, business validation, and defect triage.
Run hypercare after each migration, drive post-cutover issues to resolution, confirm exit criteria, and transition entities cleanly into steady-state support.
Deliver each entity into a condition that allows Global Delivery Center teams to support it at scale, and coordinate the support transition directly with the Global Delivery Center.
Track retirement of inherited infrastructure, licensing, and contracts after migration so that legacy run cost is removed rather than carried.
Run delivery to GTech project and portfolio management standards, including backlog management in Azure DevOps, integrated scheduling, RAID management, and Tier 1 program status reporting.
Represent Core IT technical delivery in enterprise Integration Management Office forums and coordinate waves with peer tracks across Information Security, Data, People & Culture, and Finance.
Provide executive-ready reporting on progress, risk, cost, partner performance, readiness, and stabilization, calling out decisions needed rather than reporting activity alone.
Lead the workstream leads accountable for tenant consolidation, ServiceNow, data migration and archival, and network and branch office integration, setting direction, priorities, and performance expectations.
Build and develop the dedicated Grant Thornton integration team, including recruiting, onboarding, capability development, and bench depth sufficient to run multiple entities concurrently.
Define the operating model between the dedicated Grant Thornton team and partner-supplied regional capacity, and adjust it as the portfolio scales.
Lead delivery across multiple countries and time zones, working through local technology leadership and in-country resources.
Account for jurisdictional requirements in entity planning, including data residency, privacy, statutory retention, local procurement, and equipment import constraints.
Build and maintain working relationships with acquired-firm technology leadership through the transition, providing enough clarity on timing and impact for local teams to plan around the work.
Advise due diligence and pre-close assessment activity led by Enterprise Architecture and other teams, contributing integration sizing, sequencing, and feasibility input without owning the assessment.
Own the post-entity lessons learned process and convert findings into playbook updates, readiness gates, estimating revisions, and backlog items visibly reflected in the next entity’s plan.
Maintain the technical delivery playbooks, standard designs, runbooks, and readiness checklists that make each successive integration faster and more predictable than the last.
Lead cross-functional teams through ambiguity, competing priorities, and acquisition-driven timelines while maintaining controls and decision discipline.
Influence stakeholders across functions without relying on formal authority, ensuring decisions are made in time to protect the schedule.
Maintain high professional standards, protect confidential acquisition information, and communicate with clarity and precision.

Qualifications & Requirements

10+ years of experience in enterprise technology delivery, infrastructure, platform implementation, or technology program leadership, including accountability for multi-workstream delivery.
Demonstrated experience leading concurrent implementations across identity, collaboration, service management, network, and data workstreams, with enough technical depth in each to review designs and make decisions without deferring.
Experience leading Microsoft 365, Entra ID, and Azure migration or consolidation programs, including tenant-to-tenant migration and the identity dependencies that govern sequencing.
Working knowledge of enterprise network security architecture, including segmentation, cloud landing zones, hub topologies, and secure remote access.
Working knowledge of enterprise service management platforms and the configuration data, support structures, and process alignment required to onboard a new entity.
Working knowledge of enterprise data migration and archival patterns, including pipeline-driven migration and long-term retention of legacy data.
Experience directing delivery through third-party implementation partners and offshore teams, including scope definition, deliverable review, estimate challenge, and performance management.
Track record of leading cutovers for business-critical platforms, including readiness criteria, go and no-go decisions, escalation management, and hypercare.
Experience building repeatable delivery models, factory approaches, or standardized playbooks applied across multiple entities or business units.
Experience leading and developing technical leaders, including workstream or team leads.
Strong planning and program management discipline, including backlog management, integrated scheduling, dependency tracking, RAID, and executive reporting.
Experience preparing cost estimates and business cases, and managing delivery against unit-cost targets.
Ability to lead delivery across multiple countries and time zones, working through local leadership and regional resources.
Excellent written and verbal communication, including executive-level decision materials and practical direction to engineering and partner teams.
Bachelor’s degree in Information Systems, Computer Science, Engineering, Business, or a related field required; advanced degree or relevant certifications preferred.

Preferred Experience

Experience supporting merger, acquisition, divestiture, or carve-out technology integration, particularly in a serial acquirer or private equity backed environment.
Experience integrating acquisitions across multiple countries, including data residency, language, telephony, procurement, and in-country support considerations.
Familiarity with the platforms in scope, including Microsoft 365 and Entra ID, Azure networking, next-generation firewall and secure access platforms, ServiceNow, and Snowflake.

jobs.description:
We are Builders FirstSource, America’s largest supplier of building materials, value-added components and building services to the professional market. You’ll feel proud of the work you do here every day to transform the future of home building and help make the dream of home ownership more achievable. At BFS, we believe building a successful career is not solely defined by a degree. Your experience, skills, and passion are just as important, if not more so. As such, we are committed to creating a diverse and inclusive workplace that welcomes candidates from all backgrounds and experience levels.

Duties:
Partner and collaborate with business stakeholders and process owners to develop a comprehensive roadmap spanning SAP S/4HANA, SAP S/4HANA Cloud for Receivables Management, SAP Commerce Cloud, and SAP Paybacks and Chargebacks by Vistex. Lead and manage the SAP Order to Cash (OTC) process, including configuration, integration, customization, master data, and reporting for efficient delivery of sales, invoicing, credit management, pricing, delivery, and customer service. Design and implement reporting and analytics solutions for order to cash processes, leveraging SAP S/4HANA and SAP Analytics Cloud to enable data-driven decision-making and continuous process improvement. Manage the organization's IT Order to Cash processes, ensuring alignment with Builders FirstSource's business transformation strategy and principles. Manage and mentor a team of IT Business Analysts, Software Engineers and Subject Matter Specialists to ensure effective collaboration, knowledge sharing, and delivery of high-quality solutions. Develop team members' skills and career paths through coaching, feedback, and training opportunities, fostering a culture of continuous improvement and innovation. Develop and monitor objectives and key results (OKRs) for technology Order to Cash processes, establishing corresponding KPIs to track progress and measure success. Analyze KPI data, identify trends, and recommend areas for improvement to ensure continuous optimization of Order to Cash processes. Provide regular reports and updates to stakeholders and leadership, including insights and recommendations based on KPI data analysis. Apply design thinking principles to develop innovative solutions that enhance the end-user experience in Order to Cash processes, incorporating user feedback and insights for a user-centered approach. Leverage SAP Business Technology Platform’s (BTP) extensibility capabilities to innovate, differentiate, and enhance our order to cash capabilities. Supervise assigned team members (in-person and remote): plan, assig and direct work; performance management; conduct performance reviews.

Telecommuting permitted. 20% of domestic travel required.

Requirements:
Employer will accept a Bachelor’s degree in Electronics Engineering, Computer Science, or related field and 72 months of progressive, post-baccalaureate experience in the job offered or in a related occupation.

Position Requires

Configuration of SAP Sales & Distribution, Order to Cash, SAP Commerce Cloud, and Receivables Management;
Business/Financial Management;
Product Development;
Solution Design;
Contract Management;
Data Management and Enterprise Integration Technology platforms;
Data modeling and integration frameworks; and
IT Practices and Frameworks: ITIL, SDLC, or Agile.

This position was posted on 8/21/2026 and we anticipate it will be open for a minimum of five days, though it may be open for a longer period. We encourage your prompt application.

Successful, innovative, and fulfilling careers are built here, and your professional development is a high priority. We invest in your future through the latest training, tools, and technologies. Highly collaborative, we work together to solve problems and find better ways to continually grow our business and careers every day. You’ll be empowered to try new things, gain new experiences, and build a career with unlimited horizons. The scale and depth of resources that being the #1 building materials distributor in the nation provides a variety of opportunities for you to explore - all in a friendly, people-first environment. Join us to be more, do more, and build more, together at BFS.

In addition to the base wage listed, this position is also eligible to earn an annual bonus subject to changes in plan design and documents and in accordance with applicable law. jobs.title: Senior Program Manager - CTJ - Top Secret
jobs.description:
Overview

Engages with customer stakeholders to develop partnerships, leveraging broad technical expertise. Drives customer satisfaction by engaging with customers stakeholders in a positive manner, reviewing and analyzing customer feedback, and leveraging trusted relationships with key internal resources to act as the voice of the customer. Adheres to project compliance standards and requirements of the contract and accommodates customer compliance standards. Drives project initiation for projects of medium complexity by delivering a workstream within a larger project/program. Facilitates contracting process for partner resources by briefing partners, coordinating partner candidate interviews, and identifying and acclimating partner resources to the team. Develops detailed project management plan to drive predictable delivery for projects of medium complexity or supports senior colleagues in projects of high complexity. Provides review of defined metrics, proactively monitors and tracks risks, ensures timely completion and quality of deliverables, and manages stakeholder communications. Drives timely project closure by ensuring completion of project sign off tasks. Applies advanced knowledge across project management principle areas, contributes at local team-wide level to share knowledge and support others, serves as a mentor colleagues to grow identified skill gaps, and participates in cross-border mentoring and peer alignment to share lessons learned on challenging projects.

Responsibilities

Account Delivery Management

Drives and maintains obligations to customer across the delivery lifecycle including envisioning, solution development, delivery planning, cloud consumption and usage, delivery management while ensuring adherence to security best practices in partnership with Solution Area SMEs. Ensures that customer-required or market-required security certifications are active. Leads or participates in steering committee meetings with strategic customers to discuss progress toward delivery success.
Contributes to consumption activities, through others (e.g., Customer Success resources), for customers by identifying blockers to consumption goals and enabling customers, through internal teams, to get the full value of their purchases. Holds accountability for project delivery forecast.
Supports relationships with key stakeholders in the customer portfolio to ensure service delivery is on track and issues are being anticipated, identified, and managed. Communicates current view of delivery to customer stakeholders, as appropriate.
Collaborates with Sales to support contract setup, signature, compliance, and execution from deal approvals to invoicing and closure. Manages areas of fiscal responsibility within project portfolio, staying within budget while driving engagement profitability and risk management.

Business Growth

Demonstrates accountability for the financial health of a project or program (e.g., revenue attainment, accurate forecasting, cost management, and utilization, skills, and capacity planning). Identifies opportunities to accelerate and drive consumption and delivery. Owns and drives backlog risk management. Drives incremental business on top of existing projects and programs through next step proposals, conducts customer discussions related to next stage proposal (NSP) and other opportunities. Engages in the pursuit cycle to ensure deals are structured appropriately. Supports and contributes to rhythm of business (ROB) and Chief Financial Officer (CFO) forecasting.
Looks for or creates opportunities to maximize timely cloud consumption through current deliveries. Identifies new opportunities with customers and facilitates follow up conversations with customers on Consumption both strategically and operational, and to accelerate delivery or prevent delivery delays.

Closure

Applies advanced knowledge across project management principle areas to execution and delivery, contributes at local team-wide level to share knowledge and support others, serves as a mentor to less experienced colleagues to grow identified skill gaps, and participates in cross-border mentoring and peer alignment to share lessons learned on challenging projects.
Drives timely project closure by ensuring completion of project sign off tasks (e.g., system closeout updates, deletion of customer data, Deliverable Acceptance Form). Drives incremental process improvement by reflecting on and sharing lessons learned across teams, creating and suggesting improvements to intellectual property (IP), providing feedback to managers on team member performance, and conducting closeout interviews with team members.

Contracting

Facilitates contracting process for customer and partner resources (e.g., contractors, vendors) by briefing partners, coordinating partner candidate interviews, and identifying and acclimating partner resources to the team. Supports negotiation and structuring of fixed-fee subcontractor contracts with oversight from senior colleagues. Monitors and initiates Amendments, Delivery Acceptance, Proof of Delivery, and Invoicing processes. Reviews contracts according to security and data governance standards.

Initiation

Balances needs across projects in challenging situations (e.g., scarce technical resources), with support from senior colleagues as needed, and collaborates with other groups (e.g., resource managers, Global Delivery Center) on integrated planning and organization of projects.
Drives project initiation for projects of medium complexity (e.g., multiple offerings, and/or supports projects of high complexity (e.g., tailored offerings, high visibility, high impact, market making) by delivering a workstream within a larger project/program, by driving commitment of delivery resources, assigning resources, assisting in sourcing and qualifying partner resources, and creating work breakdown structures (WBSs) with delivery team.

Intellectual Property (IP)

Researches and proactively shares intellectual property (IP) and provides recommendations for improvement including submitting new IP. Holds others accountable for reusing appropriate IP and collective knowledge by enforcing use of processes and artifacts with team members.

Monitoring and Controlling

Orchestrates and oversees a broad range of project metrics on midsize to large projects with high visibility (e.g., Vice President-level). Proactively ensures adherence to key performance indicators (KPIs) and provides strategic direction to drive success throughout project lifecycle.
Discusses and confirms Microsoft change control processes at kickoff with customer. Anticipates changes and proactively addresses by probing to ensure change can happen smoothly early in the process. Tests process before initiating formal change.
Ensures timely completion and quality of deliverables (e.g., documents) and tracking of agreed upon metrics for projects of standard complexity by applying quality management techniques (e.g., benchmarking, interviews) for collecting data. Uses analyses to identify solutions to systemic issues.
Proactively manages risks (including security risks) and issues within projects of standard complexity, leveraging technical knowledge and previous experience to evaluate risks, perform qualitative analyses (e.g., probability, impact, urgency), create risk management plans, establish processes, and work with cross-functional groups and leaders to mitigate identified risks. Contributes to recovery efforts and ensures tools are updated. Manages issue closure as a high priority. Ensures that the mandatory Information Security Risk Assessment (ISRA) is completed during project initiation, is regularly reviewed, and is signed off by accredited InfoSec Delivery Compliance Leads during delivery. Reports Security and Data Compliance breaches in a timely manner (using ReportItNow and other pertinent customer reporting outlets as applicable), informing both internal and external stakeholders.
Manages stakeholder communications on project health, issues, and financial performance for mid-size to large deals throughout entire project lifecycle, tailoring communications to the audience. Tracks and maintains customer deliverables.
Manages finances for projects with mid-size to large scopes and budgets by balancing funding and resources across workstreams, performing analyses, and leveraging cost management experience and expertise. Aims to reduce cost and improve delivery margin without impact to quality or customer experience and understands impact of decisions on the broader business (e.g., profits and losses [P&L], accrual-based accounting).

Planning

Develops detailed project management plan to drive predictable delivery for projects of medium complexity or supports senior colleagues in projects of high complexity, leveraging existing materials and experience to drive scope, resources, and Microsoft project schedule in alignment and collaboration with customer plan. Ensures use of baselining, resource load balancing, and application of work effort, dependency management, contingency planning, and utilization of software (e.g., Timeline).
Establishes clear expectations and accountabilities (e.g., reconfirm scope, Responsible-Accountable-Consulted-Informed matrix) with all project team members (e.g., consultants) and stakeholders for teams of medium complexity by leading internal and external kick-off meetings (e.g., sales to delivery handoff, formal kick-off meetings). Integrates security-first mindset into expectations for self and others. Proactively engages broad set of internal and external stakeholders, including those who are impacted by project scope/outcome, but not directly involved (e.g., Enterprise Operating Unit, India Global Delivery, customer stakeholders) and engages subject matter experts in holistic planning activities, including team validation.

Presales

Contributes to pre-sales for medium-impact projects by articulating the business value proposition associated with the project/change and considering associated complexities and risks to ensure feasibility of commercial offer. Participates in review of proposed scope and assists in developing Statement of Work (SOW), Work Breakdown Structures (WBSs), estimates, preliminary risk assessments, etc. Ensures that ISD consulting deal appropriately includes Delivery Compliance, Privacy & Security (DCPS) package to fund Secure by Default activities.

Relationship Development

Engages with customer stakeholders to develop partnerships, leveraging broad technical expertise. Manages escalations or ensures resolution of escalations with customer stakeholders through tailored corrective action (e.g., education) and overcomes ambiguous situations as needed. Learns to leverage project sponsors and internal network to influence stakeholders and resolve situations.

jobs.title: Sr. Technical Program Manager - Open Source, Kiro
jobs.description:
Description

Kiro Labs is the public home for community-built projects in the Kiro ecosystem - a GitHub organization where Amazon engineers, and over time trusted external contributors, publish the experimental tools, SDKs, MCP servers, CLI extensions, and skill libraries they build on top of Kiro. Thousands of engineers already build for Kiro every day. Almost none of that work has left the building. Kiro Labs is how we open it up: a governed but deliberately low-friction path that moves internal innovation into the open, where a broader community of developers can find it, use it, and build on it.

We're looking for a Technical Program Manager to build that program. You'll own the mechanisms that turn Kiro Labs from a promising side effort into a durable, scalable incubator: the publishing pipeline, the governance model, the lifecycle, and the metrics. You'll be the connective tissue across the Kiro product team, open source strategy, security, legal, marketing, and customer success - diving deep enough technically to understand what contributors are building, and program-managing well enough to get it shipped and keep the org healthy.

Key job responsibilities

Own the publishing pipeline end to end - Design and run the intake process that takes a project from proposal to public repo fit review, security review, license and trademark review, and repo creation - and relentlessly drive down time-to-publish.
Build the governance model - Stand up the review committee, define the fit, quality, and security bar, establish decision rights and response SLAs, and document the entire workflow.
Manage cross-functional dependencies and unblock contributors - Coordinate across product, open source strategy, security, legal/IP, marketing, and customer success. Own the critical path, clear blockers, and give contributors a single, obvious place to get answers.
Own project lifecycle and org health - Define and operate the active, maintenance, and archived states, health monitoring, and the sunset process, so Kiro Labs stays a curated set of working tools rather than a graveyard of abandoned repos.
Define and report on success - Establish the program's KPIs - projects published, external engagement (stars, forks, issues, and PRs from outside Amazon), projects that graduate to broad adoption, time-to-publish, and growth in external awareness of Kiro and report progress, risks, and tradeoffs to senior leadership.
Scale the operation - Introduce automated quality and health checks, write the SOPs, and reduce manual effort so the program runs on mechanisms

About The Team

Kiro Labs sits at the intersection of product, customer success, engineering, and open source for Kiro. It's the external-facing complement to a thriving internal builder culture: the place where the tools Amazon engineers build on Kiro reach a public audience, and where a nascent external community can start to form around the product. This role brings together partners who have each carried a piece of it - open source strategy, the Kiro product team, marketing, and customer success - under a single program owner accountable for making it work.

Basic Qualifications

5+ years of technical product or program management experience
7+ years of working directly with engineering teams experience
Experience managing programs across cross-functional teams, building processes and coordinating release schedules
Experience presenting metrics and progress to goal to senior leadership

Preferred Qualifications

Experience developing and implementing KPI goals and strategies based on broader organization goals
3+ years of software development experience, or Bachelor's degree in engineering or equivalent
Experience running open source or developer community programs, including GitHub organization administration, open source release and compliance processes, and open source licensing

new_jobs.title: Director, Core IT Integration Delivery Lead
new_jobs.description:
Job Description

Grant Thornton is seeking a Director, Core IT Integration Delivery Lead to join the team. Approved office locations can be found below.

Grant Thornton GTech’s vision is centered around enabling scalable, secure, and repeatable technology integration for acquired companies. The Core IT Integration Office is responsible for integrating acquired firms into the firm’s enterprise technology environment through a standardized, factory-style model that is governed centrally, executed through partners and in-country teams, and repeatable across the acquisition portfolio.

The Director, Core IT Integration - Technical Delivery Lead owns end-to-end technical delivery across the portfolio. The role is directly accountable for five Core IT components: tenant consolidation, ServiceNow, data migration and archival, network security, and branch office integration. It leads the workstream leads who own each of those components, sets sequencing and architecture direction across them, and manages the implementation partners and in-country resources that perform the work. Seven further Core IT components are delivered by Information Security, People & Culture, and Finance. This role does not deliver those, but is accountable for the sequencing seams between them and its own scope, so that dependencies hold and no entity stalls waiting on an unmanaged handoff.

Execution is delivered through implementation partners and regional resources. The Grant Thornton team owns the standard, the plan, the readiness decisions, the quality of what is delivered, and the outcome for the business. This role directs partner delivery rather than performing it, and is expected to know the technology well enough to review designs, question estimates, validate results, and make decisions under pressure. Scope decisions anchor to four tests: security, cost optimization, standardization, and enabling Global Delivery Center support.

Essential Duties & Responsibilities:

Own the integrated technical delivery plan across the acquisition portfolio, sequencing entities into waves that balance entity priority, size, readiness, dependency, partner capacity, and business impact.
Manage concurrency across entities so that parallel execution stays within the delivery system’s throughput, and re-sequence when readiness, funding, or partner capacity changes.
Own delivery of tenant consolidation, covering migration of acquired Microsoft 365 and Entra tenants into the Grant Thornton tenant, including identity, mail, collaboration content, device management, and associated Azure subscription and workload moves.
Own delivery of ServiceNow onboarding for acquired entities, covering configuration data, service catalog and fulfillment alignment, support group structures, integrations, and transition into the enterprise support model.
Own delivery of data migration and archival, covering the Snowflake-based pipelines that feed system migrations and the durable archival of legacy data for retention, compliance, and future reuse.
Own delivery of network security, covering the Zero-Trust landing zone, regional hub readiness, segmentation, routing, and secure remote access for each acquisition.
Own delivery of branch office integration, covering connectivity, local network and endpoint baseline, site readiness, and retirement of inherited network infrastructure.
Coordinate with the owners of the remaining Core IT components, including identity directory sync, workforce systems, identity governance, security integration phases, intranet, and financial consolidation, managing dependencies and sequencing across those boundaries.
Sequence delivery to run concurrent with Information Security’s phased model rather than behind it, and manage the dependency under which full identity-driven security controls complete only after tenant consolidation.
Hold security review and sign-off as a gate before interconnect and go-live, and resist schedule pressure to bypass it.
Coordinate with the customer relationship management workstream and other capability programs that depend on Core IT sequencing, including where staffing sits outside this team.
Own and mature the integration factory model, increasing the share of each integration that runs to a standard pattern and reducing the variable component that drives cost and schedule risk.
Own the per-entity estimating model, including size banding, and maintain its accuracy by testing estimates against actuals as entities complete.
Manage cost per user and cost per entity as governed delivery metrics, working with partners and sourcing to improve unit economics as volume grows.
Prepare cost estimates, business cases, and variance analysis to support funding decisions made by Integration Office and Chief Technology Office leadership.
Direct implementation partners, systems integrators, and in-country resources through design, build, migration, cutover, and stabilization, holding delivery to enterprise standards, committed dates, and quality expectations.
Review and challenge partner designs, bills of materials, effort estimates, and delivery plans before acceptance, and confirm that what is proposed matches the standard rather than the partner’s default approach.
Support scoping, statement of work development, and commercial negotiation for integration partners, in coordination with sourcing, legal, and Integration Office leadership.
Evaluate delivery partners by region and workstream, maintaining competitive tension, regional coverage, and the ability to scale capacity up and down as the wave plan requires.
Establish readiness gates for each entity covering identity, data, endpoint, application, security, communications, and support coverage, and hold cutover decisions to documented evidence.
Lead cutover execution across workstreams, including runbooks, command center operations, go and no-go decisions, escalation paths, business validation, and defect triage.
Run hypercare after each migration, drive post-cutover issues to resolution, confirm exit criteria, and transition entities cleanly into steady-state support.
Deliver each entity into a condition that allows Global Delivery Center teams to support it at scale, and coordinate the support transition directly with the Global Delivery Center.
Track retirement of inherited infrastructure, licensing, and contracts after migration so that legacy run cost is removed rather than carried.
Run delivery to GTech project and portfolio management standards, including backlog management in Azure DevOps, integrated scheduling, RAID management, and Tier 1 program status reporting.
Represent Core IT technical delivery in enterprise Integration Management Office forums and coordinate waves with peer tracks across Information Security, Data, People & Culture, and Finance.
Provide executive-ready reporting on progress, risk, cost, partner performance, readiness, and stabilization, calling out decisions needed rather than reporting activity alone.
Lead the workstream leads accountable for tenant consolidation, ServiceNow, data migration and archival, and network and branch office integration, setting direction, priorities, and performance expectations.
Build and develop the dedicated Grant Thornton integration team, including recruiting, onboarding, capability development, and bench depth sufficient to run multiple entities concurrently.
Define the operating model between the dedicated Grant Thornton team and partner-supplied regional capacity, and adjust it as the portfolio scales.
Lead delivery across multiple countries and time zones, working through local technology leadership and in-country resources.
Account for jurisdictional requirements in entity planning, including data residency, privacy, statutory retention, local procurement, and equipment import constraints.
Build and maintain working relationships with acquired-firm technology leadership through the transition, providing enough clarity on timing and impact for local teams to plan around the work.
Advise due diligence and pre-close assessment activity led by Enterprise Architecture and other teams, contributing integration sizing, sequencing, and feasibility input without owning the assessment.
Own the post-entity lessons learned process and convert findings into playbook updates, readiness gates, estimating revisions, and backlog items visibly reflected in the next entity’s plan.
Maintain the technical delivery playbooks, standard designs, runbooks, and readiness checklists that make each successive integration faster and more predictable than the last.
Lead cross-functional teams through ambiguity, competing priorities, and acquisition-driven timelines while maintaining controls and decision discipline.
Influence stakeholders across functions without relying on formal authority, ensuring decisions are made in time to protect the schedule.
Maintain high professional standards, protect confidential acquisition information, and communicate with clarity and precision.

Qualifications & Requirements

10+ years of experience in enterprise technology delivery, infrastructure, platform implementation, or technology program leadership, including accountability for multi-workstream delivery.
Demonstrated experience leading concurrent implementations across identity, collaboration, service management, network, and data workstreams, with enough technical depth in each to review designs and make decisions without deferring.
Experience leading Microsoft 365, Entra ID, and Azure migration or consolidation programs, including tenant-to-tenant migration and the identity dependencies that govern sequencing.
Working knowledge of enterprise network security architecture, including segmentation, cloud landing zones, hub topologies, and secure remote access.
Working knowledge of enterprise service management platforms and the configuration data, support structures, and process alignment required to onboard a new entity.
Working knowledge of enterprise data migration and archival patterns, including pipeline-driven migration and long-term retention of legacy data.
Experience directing delivery through third-party implementation partners and offshore teams, including scope definition, deliverable review, estimate challenge, and performance management.
Track record of leading cutovers for business-critical platforms, including readiness criteria, go and no-go decisions, escalation management, and hypercare.
Experience building repeatable delivery models, factory approaches, or standardized playbooks applied across multiple entities or business units.
Experience leading and developing technical leaders, including workstream or team leads.
Strong planning and program management discipline, including backlog management, integrated scheduling, dependency tracking, RAID, and executive reporting.
Experience preparing cost estimates and business cases, and managing delivery against unit-cost targets.
Ability to lead delivery across multiple countries and time zones, working through local leadership and regional resources.
Excellent written and verbal communication, including executive-level decision materials and practical direction to engineering and partner teams.
Bachelor’s degree in Information Systems, Computer Science, Engineering, Business, or a related field required; advanced degree or relevant certifications preferred.

Preferred Experience

Experience supporting merger, acquisition, divestiture, or carve-out technology integration, particularly in a serial acquirer or private equity backed environment.
Experience integrating acquisitions across multiple countries, including data residency, language, telephony, procurement, and in-country support considerations.
Familiarity with the platforms in scope, including Microsoft 365 and Entra ID, Azure networking, next-generation firewall and secure access platforms, ServiceNow, and Snowflake.

Applies advanced knowledge across project management principle areas to execution and delivery, contributes at local team-wide level to share knowledge and support others, serves as a mentor to less experienced colleagues to grow identified skill gaps, and participates in cross-border mentoring and peer alignment to share lessons learned on challenging projects.
Drives timely project closure by ensuring completion of project sign off tasks (e.g., system closeout updates, deletion of customer data, Deliverable Acceptance Form). Drives incremental process improvement by reflecting on and sharing lessons learned across teams, creating and suggesting improvements to intellectual property (IP), providing feedback to managers on team member performance, and conducting closeout interviews with team members.

Contracting

Facilitates contracting process for customer and partner resources (e.g., contractors, vendors) by briefing partners, coordinating partner candidate interviews, and identifying and acclimating partner resources to the team. Supports negotiation and structuring of fixed-fee subcontractor contracts with oversight from senior colleagues. Monitors and initiates Amendments, Delivery Acceptance, Proof of Delivery, and Invoicing processes. Reviews contracts according to security and data governance standards.

Initiation

Balances needs across projects in challenging situations (e.g., scarce technical resources), with support from senior colleagues as needed, and collaborates with other groups (e.g., resource managers, Global Delivery Center) on integrated planning and organization of projects.
Drives project initiation for projects of medium complexity (e.g., multiple offerings, and/or supports projects of high complexity (e.g., tailored offerings, high visibility, high impact, market making) by delivering a workstream within a larger project/program, by driving commitment of delivery resources, assigning resources, assisting in sourcing and qualifying partner resources, and creating work breakdown structures (WBSs) with delivery team.

Intellectual Property (IP)

Researches and proactively shares intellectual property (IP) and provides recommendations for improvement including submitting new IP. Holds others accountable for reusing appropriate IP and collective knowledge by enforcing use of processes and artifacts with team members.

Monitoring and Controlling

Orchestrates and oversees a broad range of project metrics on midsize to large projects with high visibility (e.g., Vice President-level). Proactively ensures adherence to key performance indicators (KPIs) and provides strategic direction to drive success throughout project lifecycle.
Discusses and confirms Microsoft change control processes at kickoff with customer. Anticipates changes and proactively addresses by probing to ensure change can happen smoothly early in the process. Tests process before initiating formal change.
Ensures timely completion and quality of deliverables (e.g., documents) and tracking of agreed upon metrics for projects of standard complexity by applying quality management techniques (e.g., benchmarking, interviews) for collecting data. Uses analyses to identify solutions to systemic issues.
Proactively manages risks (including security risks) and issues within projects of standard complexity, leveraging technical knowledge and previous experience to evaluate risks, perform qualitative analyses (e.g., probability, impact, urgency), create risk management plans, establish processes, and work with cross-functional groups and leaders to mitigate identified risks. Contributes to recovery efforts and ensures tools are updated. Manages issue closure as a high priority. Ensures that the mandatory Information Security Risk Assessment (ISRA) is completed during project initiation, is regularly reviewed, and is signed off by accredited InfoSec Delivery Compliance Leads during delivery. Reports Security and Data Compliance breaches in a timely manner (using ReportItNow and other pertinent customer reporting outlets as applicable), informing both internal and external stakeholders.
Manages stakeholder communications on project health, issues, and financial performance for mid-size to large deals throughout entire project lifecycle, tailoring communications to the audience. Tracks and maintains customer deliverables.
Manages finances for projects with mid-size to large scopes and budgets by balancing funding and resources across workstreams, performing analyses, and leveraging cost management experience and expertise. Aims to reduce cost and improve delivery margin without impact to quality or customer experience and understands impact of decisions on the broader business (e.g., profits and losses [P&L], accrual-based accounting).

Planning

Develops detailed project management plan to drive predictable delivery for projects of medium complexity or supports senior colleagues in projects of high complexity, leveraging existing materials and experience to drive scope, resources, and Microsoft project schedule in alignment and collaboration with customer plan. Ensures use of baselining, resource load balancing, and application of work effort, dependency management, contingency planning, and utilization of software (e.g., Timeline).
Establishes clear expectations and accountabilities (e.g., reconfirm scope, Responsible-Accountable-Consulted-Informed matrix) with all project team members (e.g., consultants) and stakeholders for teams of medium complexity by leading internal and external kick-off meetings (e.g., sales to delivery handoff, formal kick-off meetings). Integrates security-first mindset into expectations for self and others. Proactively engages broad set of internal and external stakeholders, including those who are impacted by project scope/outcome, but not directly involved (e.g., Enterprise Operating Unit, India Global Delivery, customer stakeholders) and engages subject matter experts in holistic planning activities, including team validation.

Presales

Contributes to pre-sales for medium-impact projects by articulating the business value proposition associated with the project/change and considering associated complexities and risks to ensure feasibility of commercial offer. Participates in review of proposed scope and assists in developing Statement of Work (SOW), Work Breakdown Structures (WBSs), estimates, preliminary risk assessments, etc. Ensures that ISD consulting deal appropriately includes Delivery Compliance, Privacy & Security (DCPS) package to fund Secure by Default activities.

Relationship Development

Engages with customer stakeholders to develop partnerships, leveraging broad technical expertise. Manages escalations or ensures resolution of escalations with customer stakeholders through tailored corrective action (e.g., education) and overcomes ambiguous situations as needed. Learns to leverage project sponsors and internal network to influence stakeholders and resolve situations.
Drives customer satisfaction by engaging with customers stakeholders in a positive manner, reviewing and analyzing customer feedback, and leveraging trusted relationships with key internal resources to act as the voice of the customer. Manages expectations with political sensitivity by leading Success Expectation discussions with customer, and documenting, executing, and monitoring through customer and partner experience (CPE).
Adheres to project compliance standards (e.g., confidentiality, privacy, security) and requirements of the contract and accommodates customer compliance standards, including managing compliance-related complexities (e.g., high sensitivity to confidentiality). Champions compliance by contributing to knowledge sharing across teams to build compliance capability of others.

Required/Minimum qualifications

Bachelor's Degree in related field AND 3+ years experience in project management OR equivalent experience.

new_jobs.title: Sr. Technical Program Manager - Open Source, Kiro
new_jobs.description:
Description

Kiro Labs is the public home for community-built projects in the Kiro ecosystem - a GitHub organization where Amazon engineers, and over time trusted external contributors, publish the experimental tools, SDKs, MCP servers, CLI extensions, and skill libraries they build on top of Kiro. Thousands of engineers already build for Kiro every day. Almost none of that work has left the building. Kiro Labs is how we open it up: a governed but deliberately low-friction path that moves internal innovation into the open, where a broader community of developers can find it, use it, and build on it.

We're looking for a Technical Program Manager to build that program. You'll own the mechanisms that turn Kiro Labs from a promising side effort into a durable, scalable incubator: the publishing pipeline, the governance model, the lifecycle, and the metrics. You'll be the connective tissue across the Kiro product team, open source strategy, security, legal, marketing, and customer success - diving deep enough technically to understand what contributors are building, and program-managing well enough to get it shipped and keep the org healthy.

Key job responsibilities

Own the publishing pipeline end to end - Design and run the intake process that takes a project from proposal to public repo fit review, security review, license and trademark review, and repo creation - and relentlessly drive down time-to-publish.
Build the governance model - Stand up the review committee, define the fit, quality, and security bar, establish decision rights and response SLAs, and document the entire workflow.
Manage cross-functional dependencies and unblock contributors - Coordinate across product, open source strategy, security, legal/IP, marketing, and customer success. Own the critical path, clear blockers, and give contributors a single, obvious place to get answers.
Own project lifecycle and org health - Define and operate the active, maintenance, and archived states, health monitoring, and the sunset process, so Kiro Labs stays a curated set of working tools rather than a graveyard of abandoned repos.
Define and report on success - Establish the program's KPIs - projects published, external engagement (stars, forks, issues, and PRs from outside Amazon), projects that graduate to broad adoption, time-to-publish, and growth in external awareness of Kiro and report progress, risks, and tradeoffs to senior leadership.
Scale the operation - Introduce automated quality and health checks, write the SOPs, and reduce manual effort so the program runs on mechanisms

About The Team

Kiro Labs sits at the intersection of product, customer success, engineering, and open source for Kiro. It's the external-facing complement to a thriving internal builder culture: the place where the tools Amazon engineers build on Kiro reach a public audience, and where a nascent external community can start to form around the product. This role brings together partners who have each carried a piece of it - open source strategy, the Kiro product team, marketing, and customer success - under a single program owner accountable for making it work.

Basic Qualifications

5+ years of technical product or program management experience
7+ years of working directly with engineering teams experience
Experience managing programs across cross-functional teams, building processes and coordinating release schedules
Experience presenting metrics and progress to goal to senior leadership

Preferred Qualifications

Experience developing and implementing KPI goals and strategies based on broader organization goals
3+ years of software development experience, or Bachelor's degree in engineering or equivalent
Experience running open source or developer community programs, including GitHub organization administration, open source release and compliance processes, and open source licensing
